Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Hope you are both well. We're starting our internal renewal review for the platform contract that expires in January. A couple of asks from the product and infrastructure teams:

- Move the primary workload to an EU onshore tenant (data residency requirement) with 2x baseline capacity for Q1 traffic.
- Add an APAC warm-standby region (standby capacity to spin up within 15 minutes) for peak events in APAC; expected to be used ~5% of time but required for compliance.

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — EU onshore + APAC standby needs

Caroline — thanks for the clear asks and the capacity sheet. We can definitely support an EU onshore tenant plus an APAC warm-standby. High-level:

- EU onshore: we recommend Dedicated EU nodes with 2x baseline reserved capacity; this gives predictable throughput and keeps data in-region.
- APAC warm-standby: we can provision a smaller reserved pool that autos-scales to meet the 15-minute spin-up requirement; we suggest a burst band tied to the reserved pool so costs are controlled.
- KV cache persistence: short answer — yes, but it's an operational tradeoff. We can keep prefix/KV checkpoints and replicate metadata, but cross-region session continuity for in-flight KV entries depends on the client session routing. I will loop Karthik for technical detail.

I'll get a first-pass SOW and amendment to you by EOD Thursday. If procurement needs a line-item pricing sheet earlier, we can export one in CSV.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 03:40:00 +0000

Adding technical notes for the SOW (copyable into the doc):

- KV cache persistence: we support periodic checkpointing of KV to object storage in-region. During planned failovers we can attach the restored KV to the standby pool; for unplanned failovers there is a small window (up to ~30s of recent tokens) that may be lost unless client sessions use sticky routing. We will include a recommended client-side session-affinity pattern in the ops playbook.

- RTO / RPO: Expected RTO for traffic cutover to APAC warm-standby is 10–15 minutes (tests required), RPO for KV is configurable down to 30s with more aggressive checkpointing (cost tradeoff).

- Provisioning timeline: EU Dedicated nodes: 4–6 weeks from sign-off (hardware reservation + tenancy prep). APAC warm-standby pool: 2 weeks for configuration + 1 week for cross-region validation.

- Compliance: We'll provide a DPA addendum (EU onshore processing) and SOC2 evidence bundle in a shared drive link.

Karthik Iyer
Lead, Inference Operations
